## Findings
- claim-1: The supplied primary excerpt defines \[ J_v:=\Bbbk\text{-span}\{\sigma_u:u\ge v\}, \] and calls it an ideal; here the source works with a characteristic-zero field \(\Bbbk\). [source-2@L126-L139|claim=formal-document] [source-2@L328-L339|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: Assume \(A\) has Schur \(\mathbb Z\)-basis \(\{s_\mu:\mu\subseteq q^r\}\), is generated by \(h_1,\ldots,h_q\), and satisfies integral Pieri. Then \[ S=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\mu \] is an ideal of \(A\).
- claim-3: Under the additional Schur-span premise \[ J_v^{\mathbb Z}=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\mu \quad\text{inside }A, \] one has \(J_v^{\mathbb Z}=S\); after scalar extension, \(J_v=\Bbbk\otimes_{\mathbb Z}S\).
- claim-4: The supplied primary passages do not provide the needed identification between the Bruhat-span definition \(J_v=\Bbbk\text{-span}\{\sigma_u:u\ge v\}\) and the Schur span indexed by \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq q^r\). They also do not define an integral \(J_v^{\mathbb Z}\subseteq A\). Thus literal equality \(J_v=S\) is not source-grounded from the supplied material.
## Strategy
Prove conditionally that projected integral Pieri gives \(h_kS\subseteq S\); since \(A\) is generated by \(h_1,\ldots,h_q\), conclude \(AS\subseteq S\). Keep \(J_v=S\) separate: the supplied source defines \(J_v\) only as a characteristic-zero Bruhat span.

## Gaps
The supplied excerpts do not define an integral \(J_v^{\mathbb Z}\subseteq A\), identify the source ambient ring with the box algebra \(A\), or establish
\[
\sigma_u\longleftrightarrow s_\mu,\qquad u\ge v\Longleftrightarrow i^j\subseteq\mu.
\]
Thus they do not source-ground \(J_v=S\). The conditional assertion \(J_v^{\mathbb Z}=S\) is tautological, not a proof of this identification.

## Next
Obtain an exact source statement giving either the required Bruhat-to-partition correspondence or a Schur generating/spanning description of \(J_v\), together with its coefficient-ring and ambient-ring identification. Then define the integral form and compare it to \(S\).
